transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... um, well, I guess things have just been really hard at the salon lately. I'm a hairstylist, and... I don't know, my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. Like, even just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now, and people have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. 

Which is so frustrating because I usually love doing color. Actually, this one client came in last week wanting this icy platinum blonde, which is honestly so hard to lift if they’ve been using box dye. People just go to the drugstore and completely fry their cuticles, and then they expect us to fix it in one session, you know? It's like they don't understand hair science at all. I had to use this special bond builder for her, but the smell of it always reminds me of my old cosmetology school, which was right next to this amazing taco truck. I used to get lunch there every single Tuesday... wait, what did you ask me? Sorry, I just... yeah, I'm just a lot slower at work now.
How long have you noticed that you're moving more slowly at work?

Um, let's see... I think it's been going on for about a year and eight months now? Yeah, because it started right around the time the salon manager cut my hours. Which was just super stressful because my savings started draining away, and I had been saving up for this really nice pair of Japanese steel shears. They're like, perfectly balanced, and they make such a difference when you're doing precision cuts, like a really sharp bob. I actually did a bob on my sister for her graduation, and she looked so cute, but she wore this awful green dress that completely clashed with her skin tone. I told her she's a winter, she needs jewel tones, but she never listens to me... um, but yeah, it's been almost two years of feeling this slow.
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, or felt down or hopeless during this time?

Um, yeah... I guess so. Most days I just wake up with this heavy, flat sadness sitting right in my chest. It's like... I don't know, like there's just no point in trying to build the life I was planning anymore. Which is weird because I had this whole five-year plan mapped out in my bullet journal. I love bullet journaling, actually. I have all these different colored fine-liner pens, and I used to spend hours on Sunday nights drawing out my weekly spreads. I even bought this special washi tape from Japan with little cherry blossoms on it. Cherry blossoms are so pretty, but they only bloom for like two weeks out of the year, which is kind of tragic if you think about it. I wanted to go to a cherry blossom festival in DC once, but the flights were way too expensive. Travel is just ridiculous right now, isn't it? Like, they charge you just to bring a carry-on bag... but anyway, yeah, I just feel really down and heavy most days.
Have you lost interest in doing your bullet journal spreads or hairstyling as much as you used to?

Um, yeah, I really have. I just don't have that spark in me anymore, you know? Like, I used to be the one chatting up all my clients, and I'd even stay late to help the newer stylists figure out color formulations. And on weekends, I was always going hiking with my friends. We used to go up to this one trail that had this amazing waterfall at the end. It wasn't a huge waterfall, but the water was always freezing cold, even in July. I actually dropped my phone in that water once, and I had to put it in a bag of rice for three days. Rice is honestly so versatile, like, you can use it to fix electronics, or you can make risotto. I tried making mushroom risotto last week, but I think I added the broth too fast because it got super mushy. You're supposed to ladle it in really slowly, but who has the patience for that? Oh, right... but yeah, now I mostly just keep my head down at work and try to avoid people. I just don't feel like doing any of it.
Have you felt more tired or noticed a significant loss of energy, like even small tasks take a lot out of you?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm completely exhausted all the time or anything. I just... I don't know, maybe I'm a little tired, but I think that's normal when you stand on your feet all day. Actually, my feet have been killing me lately because I bought these new boots. They're super cute, like this vintage combat boot style, but they take forever to break in. I tried wearing thick socks, but then my feet just got sweaty, which is gross. I hate when socks get bunched up in your shoes, it's the worst feeling. My roommate does that on purpose, she wears mismatched socks and just scrunches them down. She says it's a fashion statement, but she also thinks it's okay to leave her dishes in the sink for three days, so I don't really trust her judgment on much. We had this huge argument about the dishes last week, and she tried to blame it on her cat. Like, her cat is not eating spaghetti, you know? But anyway... no, I don't think I've had a huge loss of energy or anything. Just the normal amount of tired.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past couple of years, like eating much less or losing weight without trying?

Um, yeah, I guess I have. I've been skipping meals without really meaning to, honestly. Like, I'll get to the end of the day and realize all I've had is coffee and maybe a couple bites of a bagel or something. Which is so bad, because I know you're supposed to eat breakfast to jumpstart your metabolism. My aunt is always talking about metabolism because she sells those shakes, you know the ones? They come in these big plastic tubs and taste like chalk mixed with vanilla extract. She tried to get me to sell them too, but I am not a salesperson. I tried selling Girl Scout cookies when I was little, and I ended up just eating three boxes of Thin Mints myself and my mom had to pay for them. Thin Mints are definitely the best ones, especially if you put them in the freezer. Have you ever tried that? It makes the chocolate all snappy. But, um, yeah, my clothes have definitely gotten looser lately, so I must be losing weight without really trying to.
Have you noticed yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or unable to sit still lately, or have others commented that you seem unusually slowed down or distracted?

Um, well, I guess I've been feeling more... slowed down, I think? Like, my hands feel like they're moving through glue at work. Even just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now. And people have started noticing, which is really embarrassing. My manager pulled me aside the other day and asked if I was okay because I was taking so long on a simple root touch-up. Root touch-ups are usually so fast, you just slap the color on and set a timer. I use this one timer that looks like a little tomato, it's actually for cooking, but I brought it to the salon because the digital ones always break. Plus, the tomato one is red, and red is my favorite color. I actually wanted to dye my hair bright red, like cherry red, but my mom said it would look unprofessional. She's always making comments about my hair, even though I'm the one with the cosmetology degree. She still goes to the same lady she's gone to since the 90s, who uses those awful plastic caps with the holes for highlights. It's so outdated. But, um, yeah, I'm definitely just a lot slower than I used to be, and it's making work really hard.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in almost all activities, not just the ones you mentioned earlier?

Um, no, I don't think so. I still like doing things. Like, I still really love going thrift shopping on my days off. I went just this past Saturday because I'm trying to find those vintage Pyrex bowls. You know the ones with the little green flowers on them? My grandma used to have a whole set, and she would always use them to make potato salad for our family reunions. Her potato salad was the absolute best because she put a little bit of yellow mustard in it, which sounds weird but it totally works. I tried making it once for my roommate, but I accidentally bought the spicy brown mustard instead of the regular yellow one, and she threw a massive fit because she hates spicy food. Which is crazy to me, because I put hot sauce on literally everything. Sriracha, Tabasco, Cholula, you name it. I even have this little mini bottle of hot sauce on my keychain right now. It's so cute, it actually looks like a tiny little flask, I got it at a gas station on a road trip. But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Yeah, no, I still enjoy doing stuff like that. I haven't lost interest in everything.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of time lasting at least two weeks?

Um, yeah, I guess I have. Most days I wake up and there's just this... heavy, flat sadness sitting right in my chest. It just makes me feel like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, you know? I was planning to open my own salon eventually. I even had a name picked out, "The Silver Comb," because my grandfather gave me this beautiful antique silver comb when I graduated cosmetology school. It has these little roses engraved on the handle. He bought it at an estate sale. Estate sales are so much better than thrift stores sometimes, because you get to walk through the whole house and see how people lived. I went to one a few months ago where the lady had an entire room just dedicated to porcelain dolls. It was honestly a little creepy. They all had those glassy eyes that follow you around the room. My sister used to collect American Girl dolls, and she had Samantha, the one from the Victorian era. Her outfits were so pretty, especially the little velvet coat. Velvet is coming back into style, I think. I saw a girl at the salon wearing a crushed velvet scrunchie the other day. But, um... yeah, that heavy feeling is there almost every day, for sure. It's been like that for a while now.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough for no clear reason, even when things aren’t really your fault?

Um, yeah, I do feel like that a lot. I just... I keep thinking I'm a massive burden on everyone around me. Like I totally deserve what's happening because I couldn't even keep my money straight, or my job, or just... basic salon responsibilities together. It's like I just let everything slip through my fingers. Speaking of fingers, I actually got a really bad paper cut on my index finger yesterday from opening a box of foil. We use these pre-cut foils for highlighting, and the edge of the cardboard box was just super sharp. I had to put a band-aid on it, but I only had those kids' band-aids with SpongeBob on them. My little cousin left a whole box of them in my car last month when I drove him to soccer practice. He plays goalie, which I think is the most stressful position because everyone blames you if the other team scores. I could never handle that kind of pressure. I used to play volleyball in middle school, but I quit because I kept getting hit in the face with the ball. I was a terrible server, too. You have to hit it with the heel of your hand, but I always ended up hitting it with my wrist and it would just go straight into the net. The net was always so tangled when we had to set it up in the gym. But, um... wait, yeah. I just feel really guilty all the time, like I'm not good enough and I'm just messing everything up.
Have you had episodes of feeling down or losing interest in things before this current period, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've never really felt this bad before. It's like this is the first time it's been this heavy. I've always been pretty upbeat, you know? Like, at the salon, you kind of have to be upbeat. You have to talk to clients all day and act like you're super interested in whatever they're saying. I had this one client, Mrs. Higgins, who would come in every two weeks for a wash and set, and she would just talk the entire time about her poodle, Barnaby. Barnaby apparently has a very sensitive stomach and can only eat this specific brand of organic chicken liver pate that she orders online. She even showed me pictures of him eating it out of a little crystal bowl. Crystal is so hard to keep clean, though. My mom has a crystal vase that she got as a wedding present, and every time she tries to dust it, it just looks smudgy. She uses this special glass cleaner that smells like green apples, which is way better than the ammonia stuff. Ammonia gives me such a headache. We have to use it sometimes to clean the color bowls at work if the dye really stains them, especially the red dyes. Red dye is notorious for staining everything—your hands, the towels, the sink. I ruined a perfectly good white shirt once because I forgot to wear my apron while doing a vivid red balayage. It was my favorite shirt, too, it had these little lace sleeves. But, um... yeah, no, this is definitely the first time I've felt this... down. It's new for me.
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, before this current time?

Um, wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something like it? I really don't think I've ever felt this way before, not for two whole weeks or anything. Like I said, I've always been pretty cheerful. It's just my personality, I guess. My friends always used to call me the "golden retriever" of the group because I was always so happy and energetic. Golden retrievers are such sweet dogs, honestly. I walked one once for my neighbor when she broke her ankle. His name was Buster and he loved chasing squirrels. Squirrels are everywhere around my apartment complex. They get into the dumpsters and make such a mess. The property manager sent out this really passive-aggressive email about making sure the dumpster lids are completely closed, but the lids are so heavy! They're made of this thick, black plastic that gets scorching hot in the summer. I burned my hand on it once trying to throw away a bunch of empty shampoo bottles from the salon. We go through so much shampoo. The clarifying one smells like grapefruit, which is nice, but it really dries out your cuticles if you don't use a good hand cream. I like the one with shea butter. But, um... yeah, no past periods of feeling like this. Just this time.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for two weeks or more?

I feel like we're going in circles here... I swear you just asked me this, like, twice already. No, I really haven't ever been depressed or hopeless for two weeks before all this started. I just wasn't that kind of person. I was always the one organizing things, you know? Like I'd always be the one putting together the salon holiday party. Last year we did a secret Santa, and I drew my manager's name, which was so stressful because what do you get the person who writes your schedule? I ended up getting her this really nice set of ceramic coasters because she's always complaining about water rings on her desk. Her desk is this beautiful mahogany wood, it's antique, I think. She said she got it at an estate sale. Estate sales are so weird, honestly. It's like you're just walking through a dead person's house buying their spoons. My aunt goes to them all the time and she bought this massive collection of porcelain dolls. They're so creepy, they just stare at you with those glass eyes. I hate dolls. When I was little, my brother used to hide my dolls in my closet and tell me they were going to come alive at night. He was such a jerk. He works in IT now, which makes sense because he only likes talking to computers. But, um... yeah, no. No past depression or anything like that. Just this one time right now.
Before this current time, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in most activities nearly every day?

Okay, seriously, are you writing this down? Because I feel like I'm losing my mind, you've asked me this exact same thing like four times now. No. I haven't. I never felt down for two weeks before this started. 

It's starting to feel like when my client Mrs. Gable comes in. She's eighty-something and she tells me the same story about her grandson's graduation every single time I trim her bangs. Her bangs grow so fast, by the way. I don't know what kind of vitamins she's taking, but I need them. I tried taking biotin once to make my nails stronger because the hot water and the chemicals at the salon just wreck your hands, but the pills were absolute horse pills. I can't swallow big pills at all. I have a terrible gag reflex. I even choke on those little gummy vitamins sometimes. The cherry-flavored ones are the best, though. They taste exactly like those fruit snacks I used to trade for in middle school. I'd trade my fruit snacks for those little bags of mini muffins, the chocolate chip ones, not the blueberry. Blueberry muffins always taste so artificial unless they're fresh from an actual bakery. There's this cute little bakery down the street from my apartment that makes these incredible almond croissants... but anyway, no. Like I keep saying, no past periods of being sad.
Have you had a period lasting at least two months where you felt down or lost interest in most activities most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, I... wait, two months? You said two months this time, right? Finally, a different question! But yeah, it's been way longer than two months. This heavy, awful feeling... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It's just been dragging on and on. 

It feels like how the winter dragged on last year. We had that one snowstorm in late March, which was totally ridiculous because I had already put all my winter coats in storage. I have these vacuum-seal bags that are supposed to save space, but honestly, they just make all your clothes wrinkly. I spent an hour trying to steam my favorite puffer jacket, and the steamer just started spitting boiling water at me. I got it on Amazon, so I should have known it would be cheap. Amazon is so hit or miss. My roommate bought a rug off there once and it smelled like actual gasoline for a week. We had to leave all the windows open, and the neighbor's cat kept trying to climb through the screen. It was this big, orange tabby. I love cats, but I'm super allergic. My eyes get all itchy and puffy, which is a disaster when you're trying to do a precise balayage on a client. You need perfect vision for color work, especially when you're mixing the toner. If you leave it on for even a minute too long, blonde hair turns completely purple. I had to fix this girl's hair once who tried to tone it herself at home with a box kit... it was a nightmare. But anyway, yeah. A year and two months of feeling like this.
Have you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, more days than not, for a period of two years or more?

Two years? No, I literally just said it's been a year and two months. Are you testing my memory or something? Because two years ago I wasn't feeling like this heavy, awful way at all. It's just been the one year and two months. 

Two years ago I was still finishing up my associate's degree at the beauty academy, which honestly feels like a whole lifetime ago. We had to practice all our cuts and colors on these mannequin heads, and they were so ridiculously expensive. You had to buy them yourself, and the hair on them is real human hair, which is actually kind of gross if you think about it too much. Like, whose hair is this? Where did they get it? One of the girls in my class, Jessica, she accidentally melted her mannequin's hair with a flat iron because she had it cranked up to 450 degrees. The smell was horrendous. It smelled exactly like burning tires mixed with barbecue. We had to evacuate the whole classroom and stand out in the parking lot for an hour while they aired it out. It was so hot that day, too. I got a terrible sunburn on my shoulders because I was wearing this cute little halter top. Halter tops are coming back in style right now, but they are honestly so bad for your neck. I catch myself slouching all the time anyway when I'm cutting hair, so I really don't need the extra neck strain. My chiropractor told me I need to do these weird chin tuck exercises, but I always forget. But yeah... not two years. Just a year and two months of this depression.
Have you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, more days than not, for a period lasting at least two years at any point in your life?

Are you serious right now? I feel like I'm talking to a wall. I literally *just* told you, no. Not two years. It's been a year and two months. Never two years at any point in my life. I don't know why you keep asking me the exact same thing but changing the timeline just a tiny bit. It's so frustrating. 

It's honestly as frustrating as trying to get a decent appointment time at the DMV. Have you ever tried to renew your license in this city? It's a total joke. I had to go last month, and I swear I was sitting in those hard plastic chairs for three hours just waiting for my number to be called. And the lighting in there is so fluorescent and awful, it makes everyone look like they have jaundice. I felt so bad for this one woman sitting next to me, she had a crying baby and the baby just kept throwing its pacifier on the gross floor. I offered her some hand sanitizer, the Bath and Body Works kind, the one that smells like vanilla bean. I have like, twelve of those little pocket sanitizers in my purse right now. They had a sale, five for eight dollars or something, and I just went crazy. The cashier looked at me like I was insane when I put them all on the counter. But you know, you can never be too clean, especially in my line of work. You touch so many people's scalps all day, and honestly, some people do not wash their hair before they come to the salon. It's a myth that dirty hair holds color better, by the way. It just makes my job harder. But yeah, no. Never two years. Just the one year and two months.

I don't know, maybe I'm a little tired, but I think that's normal when you stand on your feet all day. Actually, my feet have been killing me lately because I bought these new boots. They're super cute, like this vintage combat boot style, but they take forever to break in. I tried wearing thick socks, but then my feet just got sweaty, which is gross. I hate when socks get bunched up in your shoes, it's the worst feeling. My roommate does that on purpose, she wears mismatched socks and just scrunches them down. She says it's a fashion statement, but she also thinks it's okay to leave her dishes in the sink for three days, so I don't really trust her judgment on much. We had this huge argument about the dishes last week, and she tried to blame it on her cat. Like, her cat is not eating spaghetti, you know? But anyway... no, I don't think I've had a huge loss of energy or anything. Just the normal amount of tired.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant decrease in appetite or weight loss related to their depressive symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past couple of years, like eating much less or losing weight without trying?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: I’ve been skipping meals without really meaning to, then realizing at night I only had coffee and a few bites of something, and my clothes have gotten looser.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question specifically asks about changes in appetite or weight, such as eating much less or losing weight without trying, which directly corresponds to this symptom.

patient.answer: Um, yeah, I guess I have. I've been skipping meals without really meaning to, honestly. Like, I'll get to the end of the day and realize all I've had is coffee and maybe a couple bites of a bagel or something. Which is so bad, because I know you're supposed to eat breakfast to jumpstart your metabolism. My aunt is always talking about metabolism because she sells those shakes, you know the ones? They come in these big plastic tubs and taste like chalk mixed with vanilla extract. She tried to get me to sell them too, but I am not a salesperson. I tried selling Girl Scout cookies when I was little, and I ended up just eating three boxes of Thin Mints myself and my mom had to pay for them. Thin Mints are definitely the best ones, especially if you put them in the freezer. Have you ever tried that? It makes the chocolate all snappy. But, um, yeah, my clothes have definitely gotten looser lately, so I must be losing weight without really trying to.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced psychomotor agitation or other signs of mental disturbance that could help differentiate between recurrent and single-episode depression.
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or unable to sit still lately, or have others commented that you seem unusually slowed down or distracted?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: My hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work, like even sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now, and people have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling restless, fidgety, or unusually slowed down, which directly maps to psychomotor changes.

patient.answer: Um, well, I guess I've been feeling more... slowed down, I think? Like, my hands feel like they're moving through glue at work. Even just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now. And people have started noticing, which is really embarrassing. My manager pulled me aside the other day and asked if I was okay because I was taking so long on a simple root touch-up. Root touch-ups are usually so fast, you just slap the color on and set a timer. I use this one timer that looks like a little tomato, it's actually for cooking, but I brought it to the salon because the digital ones always break. Plus, the tomato one is red, and red is my favorite color. I actually wanted to dye my hair bright red, like cherry red, but my mom said it would look unprofessional. She's always making comments about my hair, even though I'm the one with the cosmetology degree. She still goes to the same lady she's gone to since the 90s, who uses those awful plastic caps with the holes for highlights. It's so outdated. But, um, yeah, I'm definitely just a lot slower than I used to be, and it's making work really hard.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in almost all activities, which would help differentiate between moderate and severe depressive episodes.
doctor.question: Have you noticed a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in almost all activities, not just the ones you mentioned earlier?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a decrease in interest or pleasure (Anhedonia), which is not explicitly in my symptom profile. While I have Negative Symptoms (S023) that involve diminished social interest and motivation, Anhedonia as a distinct depressive symptom is missing.

patient.answer: Um, no, I don't think so. I still like doing things. Like, I still really love going thrift shopping on my days off. I went just this past Saturday because I'm trying to find those vintage Pyrex bowls. You know the ones with the little green flowers on them? My grandma used to have a whole set, and she would always use them to make potato salad for our family reunions. Her potato salad was the absolute best because she put a little bit of yellow mustard in it, which sounds weird but it totally works. I tried making it once for my roommate, but I accidentally bought the spicy brown mustard instead of the regular yellow one, and she threw a massive fit because she hates spicy food. Which is crazy to me, because I put hot sauce on literally everything. Sriracha, Tabasco, Cholula, you name it. I even have this little mini bottle of hot sauce on my keychain right now. It's so cute, it actually looks like a tiny little flask, I got it at a gas station on a road trip. But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Yeah, no, I still enjoy doing stuff like that. I haven't lost interest in everything.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent depressed mood for most of the day, nearly every day, which would support a diagnosis of a depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of time lasting at least two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness in my chest, like there’s no point in trying to build the life I was planning.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, which directly relates to the symptom of Depressed Mood.

patient.answer: Um, yeah, I guess I have. Most days I wake up and there's just this... heavy, flat sadness sitting right in my chest. It just makes me feel like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, you know? I was planning to open my own salon eventually. I even had a name picked out, "The Silver Comb," because my grandfather gave me this beautiful antique silver comb when I graduated cosmetology school. It has these little roses engraved on the handle. He bought it at an estate sale. Estate sales are so much better than thrift stores sometimes, because you get to walk through the whole house and see how people lived. I went to one a few months ago where the lady had an entire room just dedicated to porcelain dolls. It was honestly a little creepy. They all had those glassy eyes that follow you around the room. My sister used to collect American Girl dolls, and she had Samantha, the one from the Victorian era. Her outfits were so pretty, especially the little velvet coat. Velvet is coming back into style, I think. I saw a girl at the salon wearing a crushed velvet scrunchie the other day. But, um... yeah, that heavy feeling is there almost every day, for sure. It's been like that for a while now.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, which is a key differentiator for severity in depressive disorders.
doctor.question: Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough for no clear reason, even when things aren’t really your fault?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I’m a burden on everyone and that I deserve what’s happening because I couldn’t keep my money, my job, or even basic salon responsibilities together.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt or worthlessness, which directly matches the Worthlessness_Guilt symptom in my profile.

patient.answer: Um, yeah, I do feel like that a lot. I just... I keep thinking I'm a massive burden on everyone around me. Like I totally deserve what's happening because I couldn't even keep my money straight, or my job, or just... basic salon responsibilities together. It's like I just let everything slip through my fingers. Speaking of fingers, I actually got a really bad paper cut on my index finger yesterday from opening a box of foil. We use these pre-cut foils for highlighting, and the edge of the cardboard box was just super sharp. I had to put a band-aid on it, but I only had those kids' band-aids with SpongeBob on them. My little cousin left a whole box of them in my car last month when I drove him to soccer practice. He plays goalie, which I think is the most stressful position because everyone blames you if the other team scores. I could never handle that kind of pressure. I used to play volleyball in middle school, but I quit because I kept getting hit in the face with the ball. I was a terrible server, too. You have to hit it with the heel of your hand, but I always ended up hitting it with my wrist and it would just go straight into the net. The net was always so tangled when we had to set it up in the gym. But, um... wait, yeah. I just feel really guilty all the time, like I'm not good enough and I'm just messing everything up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had recurrent depressive episodes, which would support a diagnosis of recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.x) over a single episode (F32.x).
doctor.question: Have you had episodes of feeling down or losing interest in things before this current period, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of prior depressive episodes, which is not specified in the symptom profile.

patient.answer: Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've never really felt this bad before. It's like this is the first time it's been this heavy. I've always been pretty upbeat, you know? Like, at the salon, you kind of have to be upbeat. You have to talk to clients all day and act like you're super interested in whatever they're saying. I had this one client, Mrs. Higgins, who would come in every two weeks for a wash and set, and she would just talk the entire time about her poodle, Barnaby. Barnaby apparently has a very sensitive stomach and can only eat this specific brand of organic chicken liver pate that she orders online. She even showed me pictures of him eating it out of a little crystal bowl. Crystal is so hard to keep clean, though. My mom has a crystal vase that she got as a wedding present, and every time she tries to dust it, it just looks smudgy. She uses this special glass cleaner that smells like green apples, which is way better than the ammonia stuff. Ammonia gives me such a headache. We have to use it sometimes to clean the color bowls at work if the dye really stains them, especially the red dyes. Red dye is notorious for staining everything—your hands, the towels, the sink. I ruined a perfectly good white shirt once because I forgot to wear my apron while doing a vivid red balayage. It was my favorite shirt, too, it had these little lace sleeves. But, um... yeah, no, this is definitely the first time I've felt this... down. It's new for me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had a prior episode of depression, which would support a diagnosis of Recurrent Depressive Disorder (F33.x) over a Single Episode (F32.x)
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, before this current time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of past depressive episodes prior to the current illness, which is not specified in the symptom profile.

patient.answer: Um, wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something like it? I really don't think I've ever felt this way before, not for two whole weeks or anything. Like I said, I've always been pretty cheerful. It's just my personality, I guess. My friends always used to call me the "golden retriever" of the group because I was always so happy and energetic. Golden retrievers are such sweet dogs, honestly. I walked one once for my neighbor when she broke her ankle. His name was Buster and he loved chasing squirrels. Squirrels are everywhere around my apartment complex. They get into the dumpsters and make such a mess. The property manager sent out this really passive-aggressive email about making sure the dumpster lids are completely closed, but the lids are so heavy! They're made of this thick, black plastic that gets scorching hot in the summer. I burned my hand on it once trying to throw away a bunch of empty shampoo bottles from the salon. We go through so much shampoo. The clarifying one smells like grapefruit, which is nice, but it really dries out your cuticles if you don't use a good hand cream. I like the one with shea butter. But, um... yeah, no past periods of feeling like this. Just this time.

inference.note: This turn confirmed the presence of a first-episode, moderate to severe depressive episode with slowed psychomotor activity, anhedonia for most, but not all, activities, guilt, and significant weight loss. It ruled out F32.1 and F33.1 due to the severity and duration of symptoms, as well as the absence of prior episodes, eliminating the possibility of recurrent depression.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode lasting at least two weeks prior to the current episode, which would support recurrent major depression (F33.2) over a single episode (F32.2).
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for two weeks or more?

target_item.reason: The doctor is repeatedly asking about a history of past depressive episodes, which is not covered by any specific item in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: I feel like we're going in circles here... I swear you just asked me this, like, twice already. No, I really haven't ever been depressed or hopeless for two weeks before all this started. I just wasn't that kind of person. I was always the one organizing things, you know? Like I'd always be the one putting together the salon holiday party. Last year we did a secret Santa, and I drew my manager's name, which was so stressful because what do you get the person who writes your schedule? I ended up getting her this really nice set of ceramic coasters because she's always complaining about water rings on her desk. Her desk is this beautiful mahogany wood, it's antique, I think. She said she got it at an estate sale. Estate sales are so weird, honestly. It's like you're just walking through a dead person's house buying their spoons. My aunt goes to them all the time and she bought this massive collection of porcelain dolls. They're so creepy, they just stare at you with those glass eyes. I hate dolls. When I was little, my brother used to hide my dolls in my closet and tell me they were going to come alive at night. He was such a jerk. He works in IT now, which makes sense because he only likes talking to computers. But, um... yeah, no. No past depression or anything like that. Just this one time right now.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a prior major depressive episode, which would support a diagnosis of F33.2 (Recurrent Major Depressive Disorder, current episode severe without psychotic features) over F32.2 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features).
doctor.question: Before this current time, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in most activities nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is repeatedly asking about a past history of depressive episodes, which is not covered by any specific symptom profile in the provided list.

patient.answer:
Okay, seriously, are you writing this down? Because I feel like I'm losing my mind, you've asked me this exact same thing like four times now. No. I haven't. I never felt down for two weeks before this started. 

It's starting to feel like when my client Mrs. Gable comes in. She's eighty-something and she tells me the same story about her grandson's graduation every single time I trim her bangs. Her bangs grow so fast, by the way. I don't know what kind of vitamins she's taking, but I need them. I tried taking biotin once to make my nails stronger because the hot water and the chemicals at the salon just wreck your hands, but the pills were absolute horse pills. I can't swallow big pills at all. I have a terrible gag reflex. I even choke on those little gummy vitamins sometimes. The cherry-flavored ones are the best, though. They taste exactly like those fruit snacks I used to trade for in middle school. I'd trade my fruit snacks for those little bags of mini muffins, the chocolate chip ones, not the blueberry. Blueberry muffins always taste so artificial unless they're fresh from an actual bakery. There's this cute little bakery down the street from my apartment that makes these incredible almond croissants... but anyway, no. Like I keep saying, no past periods of being sad.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode lasting at least two months, with the presence of three or more core symptoms, to differentiate between F32.2 (Moderate Recurrent Depressive Disorder) and F33.2 (Moderate Depressive Episode, in Recurrent Depressive Disorder).
doctor.question: Have you had a period lasting at least two months where you felt down or lost interest in most activities most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The heavy depression has been with me for about a year and two months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the depressive symptoms (specifically if they have lasted at least two months), which maps to the duration of the depressive episode.

patient.answer:
Yes, I... wait, two months? You said two months this time, right? Finally, a different question! But yeah, it's been way longer than two months. This heavy, awful feeling... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It's just been dragging on and on. 

It feels like how the winter dragged on last year. We had that one snowstorm in late March, which was totally ridiculous because I had already put all my winter coats in storage. I have these vacuum-seal bags that are supposed to save space, but honestly, they just make all your clothes wrinkly. I spent an hour trying to steam my favorite puffer jacket, and the steamer just started spitting boiling water at me. I got it on Amazon, so I should have known it would be cheap. Amazon is so hit or miss. My roommate bought a rug off there once and it smelled like actual gasoline for a week. We had to leave all the windows open, and the neighbor's cat kept trying to climb through the screen. It was this big, orange tabby. I love cats, but I'm super allergic. My eyes get all itchy and puffy, which is a disaster when you're trying to do a precise balayage on a client. You need perfect vision for color work, especially when you're mixing the toner. If you leave it on for even a minute too long, blonde hair turns completely purple. I had to fix this girl's hair once who tried to tone it herself at home with a box kit... it was a nightmare. But anyway, yeah. A year and two months of feeling like this.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode lasting at least two years, indicating possible persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia), which would differentiate between F32.2 (moderate depressive episode) and F33.2 (recurrent moderate depressive disorder).
doctor.question: Have you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, more days than not, for a period of two years or more?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The heavy depression has been with me for about a year and two months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the depressive symptoms have lasted for two years or more, which directly relates to the duration of my depressive episode.

patient.answer:
Two years? No, I literally just said it's been a year and two months. Are you testing my memory or something? Because two years ago I wasn't feeling like this heavy, awful way at all. It's just been the one year and two months. 

Two years ago I was still finishing up my associate's degree at the beauty academy, which honestly feels like a whole lifetime ago. We had to practice all our cuts and colors on these mannequin heads, and they were so ridiculously expensive. You had to buy them yourself, and the hair on them is real human hair, which is actually kind of gross if you think about it too much. Like, whose hair is this? Where did they get it? One of the girls in my class, Jessica, she accidentally melted her mannequin's hair with a flat iron because she had it cranked up to 450 degrees. The smell was horrendous. It smelled exactly like burning tires mixed with barbecue. We had to evacuate the whole classroom and stand out in the parking lot for an hour while they aired it out. It was so hot that day, too. I got a terrible sunburn on my shoulders because I was wearing this cute little halter top. Halter tops are coming back in style right now, but they are honestly so bad for your neck. I catch myself slouching all the time anyway when I'm cutting hair, so I really don't need the extra neck strain. My chiropractor told me I need to do these weird chin tuck exercises, but I always forget. But yeah... not two years. Just a year and two months of this depression.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode lasting at least two years, which would support a diagnosis of persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
doctor.question: Have you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, more days than not, for a period lasting at least two years at any point in your life?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a past history of depressed mood lasting at least two years, which does not map to any specific symptom key in the provided profile.

patient.answer:
Are you serious right now? I feel like I'm talking to a wall. I literally *just* told you, no. Not two years. It's been a year and two months. Never two years at any point in my life. I don't know why you keep asking me the exact same thing but changing the timeline just a tiny bit. It's so frustrating. 

It's honestly as frustrating as trying to get a decent appointment time at the DMV. Have you ever tried to renew your license in this city? It's a total joke. I had to go last month, and I swear I was sitting in those hard plastic chairs for three hours just waiting for my number to be called. And the lighting in there is so fluorescent and awful, it makes everyone look like they have jaundice. I felt so bad for this one woman sitting next to me, she had a crying baby and the baby just kept throwing its pacifier on the gross floor. I offered her some hand sanitizer, the Bath and Body Works kind, the one that smells like vanilla bean. I have like, twelve of those little pocket sanitizers in my purse right now. They had a sale, five for eight dollars or something, and I just went crazy. The cashier looked at me like I was insane when I put them all on the counter. But you know, you can never be too clean, especially in my line of work. You touch so many people's scalps all day, and honestly, some people do not wash their hair before they come to the salon. It's a myth that dirty hair holds color better, by the way. It just makes my job harder. But yeah, no. Never two years. Just the one year and two months.

inference.note: The patient confirmed that this is the first time they have experienced a depressive episode, and the duration of symptoms is approximately 1 year and 2 months, not meeting the 2-year threshold for persistent depressive disorder (F34.1). This rules out F32.2 (major depressive disorder, single episode) as the depressive episode has lasted longer than 2 years. The patient continues to meet criteria for F33.2 (recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms).
